items.text: Actions are only by intentions, and every person shall have only what he intended.
items.attribution: The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him)

items.text: None of you believes until he loves for his brother what he loves for himself.
items.attribution: The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him)

items.text: Whoever believes in God and the Last Day, let him speak well or keep silent; and let him be generous to his neighbour, and generous to his guest.
items.attribution: The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him)

items.text: Whoever lifts from a believer one of the burdens of this world, God lifts from him a burden on the Day of Resurrection. God helps a servant as long as the servant helps his brother.
items.attribution: The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him)

items.text: Whoever travels a road in search of knowledge, God makes easy for him by it a road to the Garden.
items.attribution: The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him)

items.text: Wondrous is the affair of the believer: every part of it is good. If ease comes he gives thanks, and that is good for him; if hardship comes he is patient, and that is good for him.
items.attribution: The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him)

items.text: God says: My servant keeps drawing near to Me with what is beyond the obligation until I love him; and when I love him, I am the hearing with which he hears.
items.attribution: The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him)

items.text: God says: I am as My servant thinks of Me, and I am with him when he remembers Me. If he remembers Me within himself, I remember him within Myself.
items.attribution: The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him)

items.text: God says: My servants, I have placed injustice out of bounds for Myself and out of bounds between you. So do not wrong one another.
items.attribution: The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him)

items.text: If you did not sin, God would take you away and bring a people who sin and then ask forgiveness, and He would forgive them.
items.attribution: The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him)

items.text: God is more delighted by the repentance of His servant than a man who lost his camel in an empty land and then found it standing in front of him.
items.attribution: The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him)

items.text: God made mercy in a hundred parts. He kept ninety-nine with Him and sent down one, and by that one part every creature shows mercy to another.
items.attribution: The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him)

items.text: Gentleness is never in a thing without adorning it, and is never taken out of a thing without leaving it disgraced.
items.attribution: The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him)

items.text: God is gentle and loves gentleness, and He gives for gentleness what He does not give for harshness.
items.attribution: The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him)

items.text: The strong man is not the one who throws people down. The strong man is the one who holds himself in when he is angry.
items.attribution: The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him)

items.text: A man asked who most deserved his good company. He said: your mother. Then who? Your mother. Then who? Your mother. Then who? Your father.
items.attribution: The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him)

items.text: The believers, in their love and mercy and kindness towards one another, are like one body: when a limb complains, the whole body answers it with sleeplessness and fever.
items.attribution: The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him)

items.text: A Muslim is the brother of a Muslim: he does not wrong him and does not abandon him. Whoever covers the fault of another, God covers his fault on the Day of Resurrection.
items.attribution: The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him)

items.text: Seven God shelters in His shade on a day when there is no shade but His: among them a ruler who is just, a young person raised in worship, and a heart tied to the house of prayer.
items.attribution: The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him)

items.text: Shield yourselves from the Fire, even with half a date; and whoever does not have that, then with a good word.
items.attribution: The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him)

items.text: Every morning two angels come down. One says: God, give the one who spends a replacement. The other says: God, give the one who holds back ruin.
items.attribution: The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him)

items.text: Charity does not make wealth less. God adds honour to a servant who pardons. And no one lowers himself for God except that God raises him.
items.attribution: The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him)

items.text: Richness is not having many possessions. Richness is the richness of the soul.
items.attribution: The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him)

items.text: Look at those who have less than you and do not look at those who have more. That way you are less likely to think little of what God has given you.
items.attribution: The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him)

items.text: Be in this world as though you were a stranger in it, or someone crossing a road.
items.attribution: The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him)

items.text: Strive for what benefits you, ask God for help, and do not give up. The strong believer is better and dearer to God than the weak believer, and in both of them there is good.
items.attribution: The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him)

items.text: Be mindful of God and He will keep you. Be mindful of God and you will find Him in front of you. If you ask, ask God; if you seek help, seek it from God.
items.attribution: The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him)

items.text: Be mindful of God wherever you are. Follow a bad deed with a good one and it will wipe it out. And meet people with good character.
items.attribution: The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him)

items.text: Leave what makes you doubt for what does not make you doubt.
items.attribution: The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him)

items.text: Part of a person's excellence in faith is leaving alone what does not concern him.
items.attribution: The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him)

items.text: In the body there is a piece of flesh: when it is sound the whole body is sound, and when it is spoiled the whole body is spoiled. It is the heart.
items.attribution: The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him)

items.text: God does not look at your bodies or at your forms. He looks at your hearts and at your deeds.
items.attribution: The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him)

items.text: The bankrupt of my community is the one who arrives with prayer and fasting and charity, but who insulted this one, struck that one, and took what belonged to another.
items.attribution: The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him)

items.text: Whoever guarantees me what is between his jaws and what is between his legs, I guarantee him the Garden.
items.attribution: The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him)

items.text: The best of you are those who learn the Quran and teach it.
items.attribution: The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him)

items.text: Recite the Quran, for it comes on the Day of Resurrection speaking for those who kept its company.
items.attribution: The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him)

items.text: The believer who recites the Quran is like a citron: its scent is sweet and its taste is sweet.
items.attribution: The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him)

items.text: One who is at home in the Quran is with the noble recording angels; one who stumbles over it and finds it hard has two rewards.
items.attribution: The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him)

items.text: When God wants good for someone, He gives him understanding in religion.
items.attribution: The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him)

items.text: What God sent me with is like rain falling on land. Some ground drank and grew; some held the water so people could drink; and some was flat and kept nothing.
items.attribution: The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him)

items.text: The likeness of one who remembers his Lord and one who does not is the likeness of the living and the dead.
items.attribution: The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him)

items.text: Whoever says, glory to God and praise to Him, a hundred times in a day has his wrongs wiped away, though they were like the foam of the sea.
items.attribution: The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him)

items.text: No people gather to remember God without the angels surrounding them, mercy covering them, stillness coming down on them, and God mentioning them to those who are with Him.
items.attribution: The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him)

items.text: Our Lord comes down each night to the lowest heaven when the last third of the night is left, and says: who is calling on Me, that I may answer him?
items.attribution: The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him)

items.text: The closest a servant comes to his Lord is while he is prostrating, so ask much of Him then.
items.attribution: The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him)

items.text: If a river ran at your door and you washed in it five times a day, would any dirt be left on you? So it is with the five prayers: God wipes away wrongdoing with them.
items.attribution: The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him)

items.text: Prayer is light, charity is proof, patience is a brightness, and the Quran is an argument for you or against you.
items.attribution: The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him)

items.text: God, put light in my heart, light in my hearing, light in my sight, light on my right and light on my left, and make me light.
items.attribution: The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him)

items.text: His veil is light. Were He to draw it back, the splendours of His face would burn away everything His sight reached.
items.attribution: The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him)

items.text: God says: every deed of the child of Adam belongs to him, except fasting. That is Mine, and I am the one who rewards it.
items.attribution: The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him)

items.text: When Ramadan comes, the gates of mercy are opened, the gates of the Fire are shut, and the devils are put in chains.
items.attribution: The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him)

items.text: The best fasting after the month of Ramadan is in the month of God, and the best prayer after what is prescribed is the prayer of the night.
items.attribution: The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him)

items.text: The prayer dearest to God is the prayer of David: he slept half the night, stood a third of it, and slept a sixth.
items.attribution: The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him)

items.text: The fasting dearest to God is the fasting of David: he fasted one day and ate the next.
items.attribution: The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him)

items.text: Angels take turns among you, by night and by day, and they gather at the dawn prayer and at the afternoon prayer.
items.attribution: The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him)

items.text: Whoever makes the pilgrimage and speaks no obscenity and does no wrong comes back as on the day his mother bore him.
items.attribution: The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him)

items.text: One pilgrimage to the next wipes out what lies between them, and a pilgrimage that is accepted has no reward but the Garden.
items.attribution: The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him)

items.text: Hagar called after Abraham as he left her in the empty valley: did God command you this? He said yes. She said: then He will not abandon us.
items.attribution: The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him)

items.text: The noble son of the noble son of the noble son of the noble: Joseph, son of Jacob, son of Isaac, son of Abraham.
items.attribution: The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him)

source.locator: the Book of the Stories of the Prophets

items.text: We have more right to doubt than Abraham had. And had I stayed in prison as long as Joseph stayed, I would have answered the messenger at once.
items.attribution: The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him)

source.locator: the Book of the Stories of the Prophets

items.text: On that day people will go to Adam, and he will send them to Noah, and Noah to Abraham, and Abraham to Moses, and Moses to Jesus, and Jesus will send them on.
items.attribution: The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him)

items.text: They will come to Noah and say to him: you are the first messenger God sent to the people of the earth.
items.attribution: The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him)

items.text: Noah will be called and asked whether he delivered the message, and he will say yes. His people will be asked, and they will say: no warner ever came to us.
items.attribution: The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him)

source.locator: the Book of the Stories of the Prophets

items.text: Whoever bears witness that there is no god but God alone, and that Jesus is God's servant and His messenger, His word given to Mary and a spirit from Him, God brings into the Garden.
items.attribution: The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him)

items.text: I am the nearest of people to Jesus, son of Mary, in this world and the next. The prophets are brothers: one father, different mothers, and one religion.
items.attribution: The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him)

items.text: Many men have reached completeness, but among women none has except Mary the daughter of Imran and Asiya the wife of Pharaoh.
items.attribution: The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him)

source.locator: the Book of the Stories of the Prophets

items.text: Every child of Adam is touched by Satan at the moment of birth and cries out from that touch, except Mary and her son.
items.attribution: The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him)

items.text: Moses was asked who among people knew the most, and he said: I do. God corrected him for not handing the knowledge back to Him, and sent him to a servant who knew what he did not.
items.attribution: The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him)

items.text: Khidr said to Moses: my knowledge and yours take from the knowledge of God no more than this bird has taken from the sea with its beak.
items.attribution: The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him)

items.text: Solomon said: tonight I will go to my wives, and each will bear a horseman who fights for God. His companion said, say if God wills. He did not, and only one child was born.
items.attribution: The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him)

source.locator: the Book of the Stories of the Prophets

items.text: Two women lost a child to a wolf. David judged for the elder. Solomon called for a knife to divide the boy between them, and the younger cried out, so he gave the child to her.
items.attribution: The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him)

source.locator: the Book of the Stories of the Prophets

items.text: The angels were created from light, the jinn from a smokeless fire, and Adam from what has been described to you.
items.attribution: The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him)

items.text: Each of you is gathered in his mother's womb, and then an angel is sent and told four things: his provision, the length of his life, what he will do, and whether he will be fortunate.
items.attribution: The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him)

items.text: When God decreed creation He wrote in a book kept with Him above the Throne: My mercy overcomes My anger.
items.attribution: The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him)

items.text: God has ninety-nine names, one short of a hundred. Whoever takes them in and lives by them enters the Garden.
items.attribution: The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him)

items.text: Whoever stops somewhere and says, I take refuge in the perfect words of God from the evil of what He made, nothing will harm him until he moves on.
items.attribution: The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him)

items.text: Whoever recites the Throne Verse when he goes to bed will have a guardian from God, and nothing evil will come near him until morning.
items.attribution: The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him)

items.text: God, I take refuge in You from helplessness and idleness, from cowardice and miserliness, from the weight of debt and from being overpowered by other men.
items.attribution: The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him)

items.text: Let none of you die except while thinking well of God.
items.attribution: The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him)

items.text: If the believer knew what punishment is with God, no one would hope for His Garden; and if the one who denies knew what mercy is with God, no one would despair of it.
items.attribution: The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him)

items.text: Three things follow a man to the grave. Two come back and one stays. His family and his wealth come back; what he did stays with him.
items.attribution: The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him)

items.text: What is this world beside the next but as if one of you dipped a finger in the sea? Let him look at what comes back on it.
items.attribution: The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him)

items.text: Two blessings that many people are cheated of: good health, and free time.
items.attribution: The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him)

items.text: Take on what you can keep up, for God does not tire until you tire; and the deeds dearest to God are the steady ones, even when they are few.
items.attribution: The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him)

items.text: Should I not be a servant who gives thanks? So he answered when he was asked why he stood in prayer until his feet swelled.
items.attribution: The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him)

items.text: God says: this morning some of My servants believed in Me and some denied Me. Whoever said, we were given rain by God's favour, believed in Me.
items.attribution: The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him)

items.text: God, make it a rain that gives life and does good, a rain that waters and is not a punishment.
items.attribution: The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him)

items.text: He was the most generous of people, and the most generous of all in Ramadan when the angel met him, more giving than a wind let loose.
items.attribution: Abdullah ibn Abbas

items.text: Truthfulness leads to goodness, and goodness leads to the Garden. A man keeps telling the truth until he is written down with God as one who tells the truth.
items.attribution: The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him)

items.text: Three are the signs of a false heart: when he speaks he lies, when he promises he breaks it, and when he is trusted he betrays the trust.
items.attribution: The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him)

items.text: The child of Adam says: my wealth, my wealth. But your wealth is only what you ate and used up, what you wore and wore out, and what you gave away and so kept.
items.attribution: The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him)

items.text: Whoever calls people to guidance has a reward like the rewards of those who follow him, without any of theirs being made less.
items.attribution: The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him)

items.text: Every prophet was given signs that made people believe. What I was given is a revelation that God revealed to me.
items.attribution: The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him)

items.text: God says on the Day of Resurrection: where are those who loved one another for My greatness? Today I shade them in My shade, on a day when there is no shade but Mine.
items.attribution: The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him)

items.text: God says: I have prepared for My upright servants what no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no heart has ever imagined.
items.attribution: The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him)

items.text: May he be brought low who finds his parents in old age, one of them or both, and does not enter the Garden through them.
items.attribution: The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him)

items.text: A man said he had ten children and had never kissed one of them. He said: whoever shows no mercy is shown no mercy.
items.attribution: The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him)

items.text: The one who keeps the ties of kinship is not the one who repays in kind. He is the one who restores the tie when it has been cut.
items.attribution: The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him)

items.text: The best of you are the best of you in character.
items.attribution: The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him)

items.text: God has revealed to me that people are to be humble with one another, so that no one boasts over another and no one oppresses another.
items.attribution: The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him)

items.text: He came upon a woman weeping at a grave and said: be mindful of God, and be patient. Patience is at the first blow.
items.attribution: The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him)

items.text: No weariness, illness, worry, grief, hurt or distress reaches a believer, not even a thorn that pricks him, without God wiping away some of his wrongs by it.
items.attribution: The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him)

items.text: Your blood and your property are sacred among you, like the sanctity of this day, in this month, in this land.
items.attribution: The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him)

items.text: If you relied on God as He should be relied on, He would provide for you as He provides for the birds: they go out empty in the morning and come back full.
items.attribution: The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him)

source.locator: chapter on certainty and reliance on God

items.text: If you reach evening, do not expect the morning; if you reach morning, do not expect the evening. Take from your health for your illness, and from your life for your death.
items.attribution: Abdullah ibn Umar

items.text: Speak to people with what they can know. Would you want God and His Messenger to be denied?
items.attribution: Ali ibn Abi Talib

items.text: I have been put in charge of you and I am not the best of you. If I do well, help me; if I go wrong, set me straight.
items.attribution: Abu Bakr al-Siddiq

source.locator: his first address after the Prophet's death

items.text: The weak among you is strong with me until I secure his right; the strong among you is weak with me until I take from him what is owed.
items.attribution: Abu Bakr al-Siddiq

source.locator: his first address after the Prophet's death

items.text: Knowledge is better than wealth. Knowledge guards you, while you have to guard wealth. Wealth grows less when you spend it; knowledge grows more.
items.attribution: Ali ibn Abi Talib

source.locator: Short Sayings, to Kumayl ibn Ziyad

items.text: The worth of every man is the thing that he does well.
items.attribution: Ali ibn Abi Talib

items.text: The tongue of the wise man is behind his heart, and the heart of the fool is behind his tongue.
items.attribution: Ali ibn Abi Talib

items.text: There is no wealth like a clear mind, no poverty like ignorance, no inheritance like good manners, and no support like taking counsel.
items.attribution: Ali ibn Abi Talib

items.text: The world is a house of truth for one who is truthful with it, a house of safety for one who understands it, and a house of wealth for one who takes provision from it.
items.attribution: Ali ibn Abi Talib

items.text: Make yourself a measure between you and everyone else. Want for them what you want for yourself, and dislike for them what you dislike for yourself.
items.attribution: Ali ibn Abi Talib

items.text: Their speech is measured, their clothing plain, their walk unhurried. They lower their eyes from what they were told not to look at, and give their ears to knowledge that helps.
items.attribution: Ali ibn Abi Talib

source.locator: Sermon 193, on those who are mindful of God

items.text: Whoever sets right what is between himself and God, God sets right what is between him and people.
items.attribution: Ali ibn Abi Talib

items.text: Patience is to faith what the head is to the body: when the head goes, the body goes after it.
items.attribution: Ali ibn Abi Talib

items.text: The world has turned its back and is going; the next life has turned its face and is coming. Each of the two has children, so be among the children of the next life.
items.attribution: Ali ibn Abi Talib

items.text: Son of Adam, you are only a number of days. Whenever a day goes, part of you has gone with it.
items.attribution: Al-Hasan al-Basri

items.text: How often a small deed is made great by the intention behind it, and how often a great deed is made small by the same.
items.attribution: Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak

items.text: Whoever acts without knowledge spoils more than he sets right.
items.attribution: Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz

items.text: She was asked what the Prophet's character was like, and she said: his character was the Quran.
items.attribution: Aisha bint Abi Bakr

items.text: God is enough for us, and He is the best to trust. Abraham said it when he was thrown into the fire, and the Prophet said it when the armies gathered against him.
items.attribution: Abdullah ibn Abbas

items.text: Your Lord has a right over you, your body has a right over you, and your family has a right over you. Give every one of them its due.
items.attribution: Salman al-Farisi

items.text: Leaving a deed for the sake of people is showing off; doing a deed for the sake of people is setting up a partner. Sincerity is that God frees you from both.
items.attribution: Al-Fudayl ibn Iyad

source.locator: the Book of Sincerity and Truthfulness

items.text: Among the signs of leaning on your own works is that hope grows weak in you the moment you slip.
items.attribution: Ibn Ata'illah

items.text: Your wanting to withdraw when God has placed you among people is a quiet appetite; your wanting to be among people when He has withdrawn you is a fall from high aim.
items.attribution: Ibn Ata'illah

items.text: Rest yourself from running your own affairs. What Another has already taken care of for you, do not take up yourself.
items.attribution: Ibn Ata'illah

items.text: Do not let a gift withheld, after you have asked and asked again, make you lose heart. He has promised an answer in what He chooses for you, not in what you choose, and at the time He wants.
items.attribution: Ibn Ata'illah

items.text: Bury your existence in the ground of obscurity. Whatever sprouts before it has been buried comes to nothing.
items.attribution: Ibn Ata'illah

items.text: A wrong that leaves you humbled and in need is better than an act of obedience that leaves you proud and pleased with yourself.
items.attribution: Ibn Ata'illah

items.text: How is the heart to be lit up while the shapes of created things are printed on its mirror?
items.attribution: Ibn Ata'illah

items.text: Sometimes He gives you while withholding from you, and sometimes He withholds from you while giving to you.
items.attribution: Ibn Ata'illah

items.text: Nothing you look for leaning on your Lord is hard, and nothing you look for leaning on yourself is easy.
items.attribution: Ibn Ata'illah

items.text: The best of your moments is the one in which you see your own poverty, and are handed back to your own lowliness.
items.attribution: Ibn Ata'illah

items.text: The heart on its way to God is like a bird. Love is its head, and fear and hope are its two wings. When the head is sound the bird flies; when a wing fails, it does not.
items.attribution: Ibn al-Qayyim

items.text: In the heart there is a scattering that nothing gathers but turning to God, and a loneliness that nothing removes but keeping His company alone.
items.attribution: Ibn al-Qayyim

source.locator: on the needs of the heart

items.text: In the heart there is a sadness that nothing drives out but the gladness of knowing Him, and a restlessness that nothing settles but coming to rest in Him.
items.attribution: Ibn al-Qayyim

source.locator: on the needs of the heart

items.text: Repentance is the beginning of the servant's road, its middle and its end. He needs it at the end as much as he needed it at the start.
items.attribution: Ibn al-Qayyim

items.text: A sound heart is one that is safe from any wanting that goes against what God commanded, and from any doubt that goes against what He said.
items.attribution: Ibn al-Qayyim

items.text: Wasting time is harder than death, because wasting time cuts you off from God and the life to come, while death cuts you off only from this world and the people in it.
items.attribution: Ibn al-Qayyim

items.text: Thankfulness shows in the heart as recognition, on the tongue as praise, and in the limbs as work done for the one who gave.
items.attribution: Ibn al-Qayyim

items.text: Patience is holding the self back from despair, holding the tongue back from complaint, and holding the hands back from striking out.
items.attribution: Ibn al-Qayyim

items.text: Knowledge without action is a kind of madness, and action without knowledge does not happen at all.
items.attribution: Al-Ghazali

items.text: How many nights have you spent turning over knowledge and reading books, keeping sleep away from yourself. I do not know what the purpose of it was.
items.attribution: Al-Ghazali

items.text: The heart is a mirror, and the wrongs a person does are a smoke that settles on it, until in the end nothing at all is reflected there.
items.attribution: Al-Ghazali

source.locator: the Book of the Marvels of the Heart

items.text: Thankfulness is to use each thing you were given for the very purpose it was made for.
items.attribution: Al-Ghazali

source.locator: the Book of Patience and Thankfulness

items.text: The tongue is small in form, and the range of what it can do wrong is very wide.
items.attribution: Al-Ghazali

source.locator: the Book of the Faults of the Tongue

items.text: Listen to the reed as it tells its story, complaining of separations. Ever since they cut me from the reed bed, men and women have wept at my cry.
items.attribution: Rumi

items.text: Everyone kept far from his own root looks again for the time when he was joined to it.
items.attribution: Rumi

items.text: A man grew tired of calling on God, since no answer ever came. In a dream he was told: your calling on Me was itself My answer to you.
items.attribution: Rumi

source.locator: Book III, the man who called on God

items.text: There is one thing in this world that must never be forgotten. Forget everything else and remember that, and nothing is lost; remember everything else and forget that, and nothing has been done.
items.attribution: Rumi

items.text: God said to Moses: I do not look at the tongue or at the words. I look at what is inside, and at the state the heart is in.
items.attribution: Rumi

source.locator: Book II, Moses and the shepherd

items.text: Each of them put a hand on a different part of the elephant in the dark, and each described a different animal. Had there been a candle, the differences would have gone.
items.attribution: Rumi

source.locator: Book III, the elephant in the dark house

items.text: A friend came to Joseph with empty hands. Asked for his gift, he held up a mirror: what should I bring the most beautiful of men, except something he can see himself in?
items.attribution: Rumi

source.locator: Book I, Joseph and the mirror

items.text: God, if I worship You in fear of the Fire, burn me in it. If I worship You hoping for the Garden, shut me out of it. But if I worship You for Yourself, do not keep Your beauty from me.
items.attribution: Rabia al-Adawiyya

items.text: The stars are out, eyes are closed, kings have shut their doors, and every lover is alone with the one he loves. And here I am, alone with You.
items.attribution: Rabia al-Adawiyya

items.text: I have not served God out of fear of the Fire, nor for love of the Garden. I would be a poor servant if I had. I serve Him because I love Him.
items.attribution: Rabia al-Adawiyya

items.text: The believer sees his wrongs as though he sat under a mountain and feared it would fall on him. The careless man sees his wrongs as a fly that passed over his nose.
items.attribution: Abdullah ibn Mas'ud

items.text: She was asked what he did inside his house, and said: he was in the service of his family, and when the prayer came he went out to it.
items.attribution: Aisha bint Abi Bakr

items.text: He never struck anything with his hand, not a servant and not a woman, except when he was fighting in the path of God.
items.attribution: Aisha bint Abi Bakr

items.text: I served him for ten years, and he never once said a harsh word to me, nor asked why I had done a thing, nor why I had not done it.
items.attribution: Anas ibn Malik

items.text: This knowledge is religion, so look carefully at the people you take your religion from.
items.attribution: Muhammad ibn Sirin

items.text: The chain of transmission is part of the religion. Were it not for the chain, anyone at all would say whatever he liked.
items.attribution: Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak

items.text: Whoever used to worship Muhammad (peace be upon him), he has died. Whoever used to worship God, then God is living and does not die.
items.attribution: Abu Bakr al-Siddiq

items.text: People say that I narrate too much. I kept near the Prophet on an empty stomach while others were busy in the markets and on their land.
items.attribution: Abu Hurayra

items.text: Do not be ashamed to give a little, for turning someone away with nothing is smaller still.
items.attribution: Ali ibn Abi Talib
